paragraphs.text: שִׁלְחוּ־כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־הַ֖ר בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Send the lamb for the ruler of the land, from Sela toward the wilderness, to the mount of the daughter of Zion.
i18n.he: שִׁלְחוּ־כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־הַ֖ר בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃

notes.official:
*šilḥû-ḵar mōšēl-ʾereṣ* is “Send the lamb for the ruler of the land.” *kar* is singular and has no article, and it may be collective; ASV and JPS 1917 print “the lambs.” The line takes the clause as an order to send tribute, the payment in lambs that Moab made to Israel’s king under Mesha (2 Kgs 3:4). NJPS reads it differently, “Dispatch as messenger the ruler of the land,” and its note says “Meaning of vv. 1 and 2 uncertain.”

*missela‘* is the place name Sela (NJPS “From Sela in the wilderness”; the stable 42:11 “the inhabitants of Sela”). JPS 1917 takes the common noun, “From the crags.” Where Sela was is uncertain. *miḏbārāh* has the directional ending, “toward the wilderness” (ASV “to the wilderness”). *ʾereṣ* is territorial “land” (central `eretz`). Overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-16`.

paragraphs.translit: šilḥū-kar mōšēl-ʾereṣ misselaʿ midbārāh ʾel-har bat-ṣiyyōn

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־נוֹדֵ֖ד קֵ֣ן מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח תִּֽהְיֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And it shall be: like a wandering bird, a scattered nest, the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of the Arnon.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־נוֹדֵ֖ד קֵ֣ן מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח תִּֽהְיֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃

notes.official: The simile is singular in Hebrew, *kᵉʿôp̄-nôḏēḏ qēn mᵉšullāḥ* “like a wandering bird, a scattered nest.” ASV makes both nouns plural and supplies “so”; the line follows the Hebrew number. *bᵉnôṯ môʾāḇ* “the daughters of Moab” is kept (ASV, JPS 1917). The phrase may mean the women of Moab, or its dependent towns, as “Heshbon and all its daughters” means its villages at Num 21:25; NJPS has “Moab’s villagers.” The fords of the Arnon are the crossings of Moab’s northern river. The Arnon is not named in chapter 15; the verse adds it to the Moabite places of that lament.

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh kəʿōp-nōdēd qēn məšullāḥ tihyēnāh bənōt mōʾāb maʿbārōt ləʾarnōn

paragraphs.text: הביאו [הָבִ֤יאִי] עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי כַלַּ֛יִל צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ צָהֳרָ֑יִם סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים נֹדֵ֖ד אַל־תְּגַלִּֽי׃

i18n.en: Give counsel, execute justice; make your shade like the night in the midst of noonday; hide the outcasts, do not betray the fugitive.
i18n.he: הביאו [הָבִ֤יאִי] עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי כַלַּ֛יִל צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ צָהֳרָ֑יִם סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים נֹדֵ֖ד אַל־תְּגַלִּֽי׃

notes.official:
Ketiv/qere: the consonants הביאו give a masculine plural imperative, “bring”; the qere הָבִיאִי is feminine singular. The line translates the qere (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The feminine singular continues in *šîṯî*, *sattᵉrî* and *tᵉḡallî*, so the one addressed is probably Zion, the “daughter of Zion” of v. 1; *ʿăśû* is plural. English cannot show the gender.

*pᵉlîlāh* (from *pll*) is a rare noun for a decision or an arbitration. The line keeps ASV and JPS 1917 “execute justice”; NJPS has “Offer counsel” and marks it “Meaning of Heb. uncertain.” The English “justice” here does not render *mišpāṭ*, which is “justice” in v. 5.

JPS 1917 prints vv. 3–4a as quoted speech, and NJPS vv. 2–4a: the plea of Moab’s fugitives. No speaker is introduced, so the line follows ASV and prints no quotation marks (`title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: hbyʾw [hābīʾī] ʿēṣāh ʿăśū pəlīlāh šītī kallayil ṣillēk bətōk ṣohŏrāyim sattərī niddāḥīm nōdēd ʾal-təgallī

paragraphs.text: יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ נִדָּחַ֔י מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי־סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־אָפֵ֤ס הַמֵּץ֙ כָּ֣לָה שֹׁ֔ד תַּ֥מּוּ רֹמֵ֖ס מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Let my outcasts sojourn with you; as for Moab, be a hiding place for them from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner has come to an end, destruction has ceased, those who trample are consumed out of the land.
i18n.he: יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ נִדָּחַ֔י מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי־סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־אָפֵ֤ס הַמֵּץ֙ כָּ֣לָה שֹׁ֔ד תַּ֥מּוּ רֹמֵ֖ס מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
*niddāḥay môʾāḇ*: the Masoretic pointing, with the disjunctive accent on *niddāḥay*, gives “my outcasts; as for Moab” (ASV, JPS 1917), and the line follows it. Repointed as the construct *niddᵉḥê môʾāḇ*, the words mean “the outcasts of Moab.” NJPS prints “Moab’s outcasts,” with the note “Heb. ‘my outcasts, Moab.’” Whether the LXX reads the construct was not verified.

*hammēṣ* occurs only here. It is rendered “the extortioner” (ASV), probably from *mîṣ* “press, squeeze” (Prov 30:33); NJPS has “violence.” The plural verb *tammû* with the singular participle *rōmēs* is rendered “those who trample.”

paragraphs.translit: yāgūrū bāk niddāḥay mōʾāb hĕwī-sēter lāmō mippənē šōdēd kī-ʾāpēs hammēṣ kālāh šōd tammū rōmēs min-hāʾāreṣ

paragraphs.text: וְהוּכַ֤ן בַּחֶ֙סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃

i18n.en: And a throne shall be established in kindness, and one shall sit on it in truth in the tent of David, judging and seeking justice, and swift in righteousness.
i18n.he: וְהוּכַ֤ן בַּחֶ֙סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃

notes.official:
*ḥeseḏ* and *ʾĕmeṯ* stand in separate cola here (*baḥeseḏ … beʾĕmeṯ*), not as the bound pair *ḥeseḏ wᵉʾĕmeṯ*. The line therefore applies the central entry for solitary *ḥeseḏ*, `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`: “kindness,” as at 54:8 and 54:10. The pair entry `chesed-v-emet-steadfast-love-and-truth`, which keeps *chesed* untranslated inside the bound formula, does not apply. ASV has “lovingkindness,” JPS 1917 “mercy” and NJPS “goodness.” *ʾĕmeṯ* is “truth” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “faithfulness”).

*mišpāṭ* and *ṣeḏeq* are also split across cola, so they are rendered one by one, “justice” and “righteousness,” and the central `tzedakah-u-mishpat-justice-pair` is not applied (as at 5:7 and 32:16). *mᵉhîr ṣeḏeq* is “swift in righteousness,” without ASV’s supplied “to do.” The adjective also means “skilled” (Ps 45:2 Heb.; Ezra 7:6).

The verse breaks into the plea with a promise of a just throne in “the tent of David” (*ʾōhel dāwiḏ*, not the *sukkaṯ dāwîḏ* “booth of David” of Amos 9:11). NJPS notes that 14:32 “would read well here.”

paragraphs.translit: wəhūkan baḥesed kissēʾ wəyāšab ʿālāyw beʾĕmet bəʾōhel dāwid šōpēṭ wədōrēš mišpāṭ ūməhir ṣedeq

paragraphs.text: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּ֣א מְאֹ֑ד גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֥ן בַּדָּֽיו׃ (ס)

i18n.en: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and his pride and his wrath; his boasts are nothing.
i18n.he: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּ֣א מְאֹ֑ד גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֥ן בַּדָּֽיו׃ (ס)

notes.official:
Four words of the root *gʾh* fill the verse: *gᵉʾôn-môʾāḇ*, *gēʾ*, *gaʾăwāṯô*, *gᵉʾônô*. Wave rule 2 makes “majesty” the default for *gāʾôn*, but here the word names Moab’s arrogance, and “majesty” would misreport it. The line departs from the default, as the rule allows, with “pride” (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS), the word the stable 13:19 uses for *gāʾôn* (“the pride of the Chaldeans”). *gaʾăwāh* is “haughtiness,” as at 13:11 (“the haughtiness of the ruthless”), and *gēʾ* is “proud.” The decision is recorded in the overlay `gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah`.

*ʿeḇrāṯô* keeps ASV “his wrath.” The noun means an overflowing, of anger or of arrogance (Prov 21:24), and NJPS’s list ends in “arrogance.” *lōʾ-ḵēn baddāyw* follows ASV, “his boasts are nothing,” taking *bad* as idle talk. NJPS reads *baddāyw* as a suffixed preposition, “And of the iniquity in him.” NJPS prints the verse as quoted speech; no speaker is introduced, and the line has no quotation marks.

Isa 16:6–12 runs parallel to Jer 48:29–36 (overlay `moab-lament-jer-48-parallel-isaiah-16`). Jer 48:29 has six terms, *gᵉʾôn … gēʾeh … gobhô ûḡᵉʾônô wᵉgaʾăwāṯô wᵉrum libbô*, and Jer 48:30 continues *ʿeḇrāṯô wᵉlōʾ-ḵēn baddāyw*. The Isaiah line translates Isaiah’s text and does not harmonize it with Jeremiah.

paragraphs.translit: šāmaʿnū gəʾōn-mōʾāb gēʾ məʾōd gaʾăwātō ūgəʾōnō wəʿebrātō lōʾ-kēn baddāyw (s)

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְמוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ־נְכָאִֽים׃

i18n.en: Therefore Moab wails for Moab; everyone wails. For the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth you moan, utterly stricken.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְמוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ־נְכָאִֽים׃

notes.official:
The lament of vv. 7 and 9–11 is in the English present, as in the stable chapter 15, which has the same clauses (15:2 “Moab wails”; 15:3 *kullōh yᵉyêlîl* “everyone wails”; overlay `moab-lament-present-tense-isaiah-16`). ASV and JPS 1917 use the future (“shall Moab wail”). NJPS reads a jussive, “let Moab howl,” which the short form allows; it is the main alternative.

*laʾăšîšê qîr-ḥăreśeṯ* is “for the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth” (ASV, NJPS; for the word cf. 2 Sam 6:19; Hos 3:1). The parallel Jer 48:31 has the similar-looking *ʾanšê qîr-ḥereś* “the men of Kir-heres” (the phrase recurs at 48:36, which NJPS cites in its note: “Jer. 48.36 has ‘men’”). Jer 48:31 is also in the first person, *ʾêlîl … ʾezʿāq* “I wail … I cry out,” with third-person *yehgeh* “he moans,” where Isaiah has *yᵉyêlîl* “Moab wails” and second-person *tehgû* “you moan.” The line keeps Isaiah’s MT. Some interpreters take *ʾăšîšê* as “foundations.” Kir-hareseth is the Moabite stronghold of 2 Kgs 3:25, the “Kir of Moab” of 15:1.

paragraphs.translit: lākēn yəyēlīl mōʾāb ləmōʾāb kullōh yəyēlīl laʾăšīšē qīr-ḥăreśet tehgū ʾak-nəkāʾīm

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ עַד־יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃

i18n.en: For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches; they reached as far as Jazer, they strayed into the wilderness; its shoots spread abroad, they passed over the sea.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ עַד־יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃

notes.official:
The subject of *hālᵉmû* is disputed. The line follows ASV: *baʿălê ḡôyim* “the lords of the nations” strike down Sibmah’s choice branches (*śᵉrûqqehā*). JPS 1917 makes the vines the subject (“Whose choice plants did overcome The lords of nations”), meaning that Sibmah’s wine laid its drinkers low. NJPS takes *baʿălê ḡôyim* as a place name, “Their tendrils spread To Baale-goiim,” and marks it “Meaning of Heb. uncertain.”

The vine’s reach, to Jazer, into the wilderness and across the sea, is the extent of Moab’s vineyards. Jer 48:32 shortens the image (“your tendrils crossed the sea, they reached to the sea of Jazer”); the sea is probably the Dead Sea. Heshbon and Elealeh are spelled as at 15:4.

paragraphs.translit: kī šadmōt ḥešbōn ʾumlāl gepen śibmāh baʿălē gōyim hāləmū śərūqqēhā ʿad-yaʿzēr nāgāʿū tāʿū midbār šəluḥōtēhā niṭṭəšū ʿābərū yām

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֙וֶךְ֙ דִּמְעָתִ֔י חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י עַל־קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־קְצִירֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃

i18n.en: Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I drench you with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh; for upon your summer fruit and upon your harvest the shout has fallen.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֙וֶךְ֙ דִּמְעָתִ֔י חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י עַל־קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־קְצִירֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃

notes.official:
*hêḏāḏ* (here and in v. 10) is the shout of the grape-treaders, and it can also be a war cry (Jer 25:30; 51:14). ASV supplies a different word at each site, “[battle] shout” here and “[vintage] shout” in v. 10. The line drops both, so that the repeated Hebrew word keeps one English rendering, “the shout” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-16`).

In the parallel Jer 48:32 this colon reads *šōḏēḏ nāp̄āl* “a destroyer has fallen,” and it has *bᵉṣîrēḵ* “your vintage” where Isaiah has *qᵉṣîrēḵ* “your harvest.” The Jeremiah Hebrew was checked, and the first difference is also in an NJPS note. *ʾărayyāweḵ* is an unusual form of *rwh* “saturate”: “I drench you.” “I weep” is in the present, as in v. 7.

paragraphs.translit: ʿal-kēn ʾebkeh bibkī yaʿzēr gepen śibmāh ʾărayyāwek dimʿātī ḥešbōn wəʾelʿālēh kī ʿal-qēṣēk wəʿal-qəṣīrēk hēdād nāpāl

paragraphs.text: וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ מִן־הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹֽא־יְרֻנָּ֖ן לֹ֣א יְרֹעָ֑ע יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃

i18n.en: And joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field, and in the vineyards there is no singing, no shouting; no treader treads out wine in the winepresses; I have made the shout cease.
i18n.he: וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ מִן־הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹֽא־יְרֻנָּ֖ן לֹ֣א יְרֹעָ֑ע יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃

notes.official: *kerem* is “vineyard” (central `kerem-vineyard`), and *karmel* is “the fruitful field,” as at 10:18, 29:17 and 32:15–16. The negated imperfects (*lōʾ-yᵉrunnān*, *lōʾ yᵉrōʿāʿ*, *lōʾ-yiḏrōḵ*) are present, with the rest of the lament, where ASV has the future (“there shall be no singing”). *hêḏāḏ hišbattî* is “I have made the shout cease.” The first person who silences the shout is most naturally YHWH (cf. Jer 48:33, 35); whether the weeping “I” of vv. 9 and 11 is the same speaker is disputed. NJPS smooths the verb to “The shouts have been silenced” (note: “Lit. ‘I have silenced’”). Jer 48:33 has the same first person, *hišbattî*.

paragraphs.translit: wəneʾĕsap śimḥāh wāgīl min-hakkarmel ūbakkərāmīm lōʾ-yərunnān lōʾ yərōʿāʿ yayin bayqābīm lōʾ-yidrōk haddōrēk hēdād hišbattī

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃

i18n.en: Therefore my inner parts sound like a lyre for Moab, and my inmost being for Kir-heres.
i18n.he: עַל־כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃

notes.official:
*mēʿay* means literally “my innards,” the organs in which grief is felt (Jer 4:19; Song 5:4; Isa 63:15). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render “my heart.” The line has “my inner parts” because the stable 15:5 gives “heart” to *lēḇ* in the same lament (“My heart cries out for Moab”), and the translation keeps the two Hebrew words apart (overlay `meim-inner-parts-isaiah`). *qirbî* then becomes “my inmost being” (ASV and JPS 1917 “mine inward parts”; NJPS “my very soul”).

The parallel Jer 48:36 has *libbî* “my heart” twice in place of Isaiah’s *mēʿay … qirbî*, and *kaḥălilîm* “like flutes” for *kakkinnôr* “like a lyre.” *kinnôr* is “lyre,” as at 5:12 and 24:8 (ASV “harp”). *yehĕmû* is “sound” (ASV “soundeth”), the noise of the strings; “moan” stays with *hāḡāh* in v. 7.

paragraphs.translit: ʿal-kēn mēʿay ləmōʾāb kakkinnōr yehĕmū wəqirbī ləqīr ḥāreś

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־נִרְאָ֛ה כִּֽי־נִלְאָ֥ה מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַבָּמָ֑ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass, when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he shall not prevail.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־נִרְאָ֛ה כִּֽי־נִלְאָ֥ה מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַבָּמָ֑ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃

notes.official:
*kî-nirʾāh kî-nilʾāh* puts two nearly identical verbs side by side. *nirʾāh* is the Niphal of *rʾh*, used for appearing before a deity at a sanctuary (Exod 23:15, 17); *nilʾāh* is “he wearies himself.” The line keeps both, with ASV: “when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself.” Some commentators delete *nirʾāh* as a dittography (not verified for particular editions). JPS 1917 reads “when it is seen that Moab hath wearied himself,” and NJPS “when it has become apparent that Moab has gained nothing.” The line follows MT (`mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*ʿal-habbāmāh* “on the high place” matches the high places of Dibon in 15:2. The parallel at this point is Jer 48:35, where YHWH puts an end in Moab to the one who offers at a high place and burns incense to his god.

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh kī-nirʾāh kī-nilʾāh mōʾāb ʿal-habbāmāh ūbāʾ ʾel-miqdāšō ləhitpallēl wəlōʾ yūkāl

paragraphs.text: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מוֹאָ֖ב מֵאָֽז׃

i18n.en: This is the word that YHWH spoke concerning Moab in time past.
i18n.he: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מוֹאָ֖ב מֵאָֽז׃

paragraphs.translit: zeh haddābār ʾăšer dibber YHWH ʾel-mōʾāb mēʾāz

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְנִקְלָה֙ כְּב֣וֹד מוֹאָ֔ב בְּכֹ֖ל הֶהָמ֣וֹן הָרָ֑ב וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But now YHWH has spoken, saying: Within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all the great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and of no account.
i18n.he: וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְנִקְלָה֙ כְּב֣וֹד מוֹאָ֔ב בְּכֹ֖ל הֶהָמ֣וֹן הָרָ֑ב וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*kišnê śāḵîr* is “as the years of a hireling” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “fixed like the years of a hired laborer”). It means a term counted exactly, as a hired worker’s time is counted (Lev 25:50 and Job 7:1, *kîmê śāḵîr*). The same phrase sets Kedar’s one year at 21:16, and the overlay `shnei-sakhir-years-of-hireling-isaiah` fixes one rendering for both sites (wave I-4 ruling 14).

*kᵉḇôḏ môʾāḇ* is “the glory of Moab,” under the strict rule for *kāḇôḏ*. The verb *wᵉniqlāh* “shall be brought into contempt” comes from *qlh* “be light” and plays on *kbd* “be heavy”: Moab’s weight becomes lightness. *bᵉḵōl hehāmôn hārāḇ* has the article and no suffix, so it is rendered “with all the great multitude” (ASV “his”). The prose of vv. 13–14 turns the older word “in time past” into a prediction with a date.

paragraphs.translit: wəʿattāh dibber YHWH lēʾmōr bəšālōš šānīm kišnē śākīr wəniqlāh kəbōd mōʾāb bəkōl hehāmōn hārāb ūšəʾār məʿaṭ mizʿār lōʾ kabbīr (s)
